body:
# Bump vulnerable Cargo dependencies in `core-bridge` (quinn-proto, rustls-webpki, tar)

`@temporalio/core-bridge@1.15.0` ships a `Cargo.lock` with four known vulnerabilities in its Rust dependency tree. All have upstream fixes available but are not yet pulled into the SDK.

| Crate | Installed | Fixed | CVE | Severity | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| quinn-proto | 0.11.13 | 0.11.14 | CVE-2026-31812 | HIGH | Denial of Service via crafted QUIC Initial packet |
| rustls-webpki | 0.103.9 | 0.103.10 | GHSA-pwjx-qhcg-rvj4 | MEDIUM | CRLs not considered authoritative by Distribution Point due to faulty matching |
| tar | 0.4.44 | 0.4.45 | CVE-2026-33055 | MEDIUM | Arbitrary file extraction via path traversal in crafted tar archive |
| tar | 0.4.44 | 0.4.45 | CVE-2026-33056 | MEDIUM | Arbitrary directory permission modification via crafted tar archive |

## How to reproduce

```bash
trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM --exit-code 1 <any-image-using-temporalio-sdk>
```

Trivy picks up `node_modules/@temporalio/core-bridge/Cargo.lock` and reports the above findings.

## Requested fix

Run `cargo update` (or targeted `cargo update -p quinn-proto -p webpki -p tar`) in the `core-bridge` crate and cut a patch release. All four vulnerabilities have fixed versions available upstream — no breaking changes expected from these patch bumps.

## Impact

Teams running container image vulnerability scanning (Trivy, Grype, etc.) in CI/CD pipelines are forced to suppress these CVEs via `.trivyignore` to unblock builds, reducing the effectiveness of their security gates.

comments.body:
We are seeing the same `quinn-proto` CVE-2026-31812 via AWS Inspector on our production images. We've upgraded to `@temporalio/*` **1.15.0**, but since **v1.15.0** still ships `quinn-proto` **0.11.13**, the finding persists. PR #1961 (merged March 11) has the fix -- would appreciate a patch release.

Thanks
These dependencies have been bumped as of 1.16.0
